name: Dialog
import: import { Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogBody, DialogFooter, DialogClose, AlertDialog, AlertDialogTrigger, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogBody, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogClose } from "@/components/ui/dialog"
description: Modal dialog primitives for focused workflows, plus AlertDialog parts for required confirmations.

Dialog.description: Root state holder for a modal workflow.

onOpenChange.description: Called when trigger, close, escape, or outside press changes open state.

modal.description: Base UI modal behavior. Keep true for normal dialogs.

DialogTrigger.description: Button that opens the dialog. Compose with kubkit Button through render.

render.description: Use render={<Button />} so triggers use kubkit Button styling.

DialogContent.description: Portal-backed modal surface with backdrop, viewport, popup, and optional close icon.

children.description: DialogHeader, DialogBody, DialogFooter, and custom content.

size.description: Maximum popup width. Use lg for denser forms, not arbitrary max-width classes.

showCloseButton.description: Shows the icon close button. Keep enabled unless the flow must be completed with footer actions.

initialFocus.description: Base UI focus target when opened.

finalFocus.description: Base UI focus target when closed.

className.description: Layout escape hatch only; do not restyle surface, radius, backdrop, or shadow.

DialogHeader.description: Header wrapper for title and description.

children.description: Form fields, explanatory content, or workflow UI.

DialogFooter.description: Action row. Compose kubkit Button and DialogClose here.

children.description: One primary action and one secondary/cancel action.
Short title that names the workflow.
Concise explanation, not a full instructions page.

DialogClose.description: Close control. Render kubkit Button as this part for footer actions.

children.description: Close/cancel label when used in footer.

render.description: Use render={<Button variant="secondary" />} for styled close actions.

AlertDialog.description: Root state holder for required confirmations. Use for destructive or irreversible decisions.

onOpenChange.description: Called when the confirmation opens or closes.

AlertDialogTrigger.description: Button that opens a required confirmation.

render.description: Use render={<Button variant="destructive" />} for dangerous actions.

AlertDialogContent.description: Confirmation popup. Defaults to a smaller size.

size.description: Maximum popup width. Keep confirmations compact.

AlertDialogClose.description: Confirmation response control. Use for both cancel and confirm actions.

render.description: Use render={<Button />} or render={<Button variant="destructive" />} for styled actions.

disabled.description: Prevents this response while async work is pending.

forbidden: Do not create a separate ConfirmDialog component unless the app has repeated business-specific copy or async behavior to centralize.
Do not use Dialog for simple inline feedback; use Alert.
Do not use Dialog as a full page replacement on mobile; use Sheet for edge panels once available.
Do not add custom visible borders to the popup surface.
Do not put more than one primary action in the footer.
Do not hide a required close path in modal dialogs; touch screen readers need an escape control.

responsive.note: Footer actions stack on mobile and should be composed with kubkit Button. Dialog viewport scrolls when content is taller than the screen.

example:
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button />}>Open dialog</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Edit details</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Update the information shown to teammates.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogBody>{/* form fields */}</DialogBody>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <Button>Save</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
